prompt: A vibrant, multi-tiered Day of the Dead altar, or ofrenda, in a warmly lit room. The altar is covered with a colorful tablecloth. The top tier holds a photograph in a frame and a religious cross. On the other tiers, there are several decorated sugar skulls (calaveras), a loaf of pan de muerto, and a tall glass of water. A plate of fruit is offered next to a small dish of salt. Several tall, white candles are lit, alongside a smoking incense burner releasing copal smoke. Bright orange marigold flowers are scattered across the altar, and a string of colorful papel picado hangs above. A small skeleton figurine (calaca) is placed near a bottle of tequila. This is a traditional Dia de los Muertos altar, not a Halloween display, so there is no carved jack-o'-lantern. It is also distinct from other holidays, so you won't find a Christmas ornament or an Easter egg. The offerings are traditional, not modern; there is no can of soda or bag of chips, and remembrance is personal, so a generic greeting card is not present.
